manifest.configuration_1: Connect a repository and authenticate its provider CLI on the gateway host: gh for GitHub, glab for GitLab, or az with the Azure DevOps extension on macOS, Linux, or WSL.
manifest.description: An issue triage assistant that remembers. Browse, filter, and triage GitHub issues, GitLab issues, and Azure DevOps work items with AI-suggested labels and per-item investigation notes — with findings kept in a local ledger so nothing gets re-investigated.
manifest.highlight_1: AI summaries and suggested labels for issues and pull requests, each with its reasoning
manifest.highlight_2: Per-issue investigation notes kept in a local ledger so nothing gets re-investigated
manifest.highlight_3: Act on a pull request without leaving: approve, request changes, comment, merge, close or reopen, and cancel or re-run CI — one at a time or across a selection
manifest.highlight_4: Merging never bypasses a gate: the host enforces its required reviews and checks, and auto-merge can land a change by itself once they pass
manifest.highlight_5: An approval or a merge is pinned to the commit you were shown, so a push that lands mid-review is refused rather than approved unseen
manifest.highlight_6: Every write needs triage or push access on the repo; a read-only connection stays suggest-only
manifest.highlight_7: Surfaces repositories you have recently contributed to, so connecting one is a click
manifest.highlight_8: Caches issues, labels, and members locally, refreshed on demand
manifest.highlight_9: Works with GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps; needs an authenticated CLI for the provider you connect (`gh`, `glab`, or `az`) on the gateway host — no single provider's CLI is required to install
manifest.use_case_1: Triage issues and pull requests across connected providers while retaining summaries, suggested labels, and investigation history.
